t.1.124.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: O Bhārata, seeing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the sons of Pāṇḍu accomplished in weapons, Droṇa, O king, spoke to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the lord of men.
t.1.124.2: In the presence of Kṛpa, Somadatta and the wise Bāhlīka, of Gāṅgeya, of Vyāsa and of Vidura.
t.1.124.3: O king, best of the Kurus, your princes have completed their learning; with your consent, O king, let them display their own skill.
t.1.124.4: Then the great king, his inner self filled with delight, said: "Bhāradvāja, a great deed has been accomplished by you, O best of the twice-born!"
t.1.124.5: But when you deem the time right, in whatever place and in whatever manner, command me yourself, so that I may arrange it accordingly in just that way.
t.1.124.6: Today, out of despondency, I envy those men who have eyes, who will behold my dear sons displaying their prowess for the sake of weapons.
t.1.124.8: Then, having taken leave of the king, the greatly wise Bhāradvāja went outside, followed by Vidura, and had a piece of ground measured out that was level, free of trees and free of shrubs, and that sloped toward the north.
t.1.124.7: Kṣattar, whatever the guru, the teacher, says, do it just so; for I think nothing so pleasing will ever come to pass, O you who cherish dharma.
t.1.124.10: And there on the arena grounds the craftsmen built a very spacious, well-constructed viewing hall, laid out according to rule as prescribed in the treatises, furnished with every kind of weapon, for the king and for the women as well, O bull among men.
t.1.124.9: On that ground he made an offering on a lunar day honored by an auspicious constellation, and it was proclaimed throughout the city for that purpose, O best of speakers.
t.1.124.11: And there the people of the countryside had platforms built, broad and lofty, as well as costly palanquins.
t.1.124.12: Then, when that day had arrived, the king, together with his ministers, placing Bhīṣma at the front, and Kṛpa, the best of teachers,
t.1.124.13: He came to the splendid viewing hall, made of gold, hung all around with nets of pearls and adorned with beryl gems.
t.1.124.14: And the illustrious Gāndhārī and Kuntī, O best of victors, and all the women of the king, with their servants and retinues, joyfully mounted the platforms, as the wives of the gods ascend Mount Meru.
t.1.124.15: And the people of the four varṇas, headed by the brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas, came hurrying from the city, eager to behold the princes' mastery of weapons.
t.1.124.16: With the musical instruments being played and with the eager curiosity of the people, that assembly then became like a great ocean stirred into turmoil.
t.1.124.17: Then, wearing white garments and a white sacred thread, with white hair and a white beard, adorned with white garlands and white unguents, he came forth.
t.1.124.19: He, the best of the mighty, made the offering in accordance with custom, and there he had the brāhmaṇas versed in mantras recite the benediction.
t.1.124.18: Then the teacher, together with his son, entered the middle of the arena, like the radiant sun accompanied by Mars entering a sky free of clouds.
t.1.124.20: Then, immediately after the auspicious proclamation of the holy day, men entered, carrying weapons and equipment of various kinds.
t.1.124.21: Then the mighty bulls of the Bharatas entered, their armor fastened, their girdles tied, their quivers bound on, and bows in hand.
t.1.124.22: And there those princes of great valour, led by Yudhiṣṭhira, displayed their most wondrous skill with weapons, one after another in order of seniority.
t.1.124.23: Some of the men bowed their heads for fear of the flying arrows, while others watched boldly, filled with amazement.
t.1.124.24: Swiftly borne along by their horses, they pierced the targets with arrows of many kinds, adorned with the marks of their names and loosed with deft lightness of hand.
t.1.124.25: Seeing there that band of princes, holding arrows and bows, looking like a city of the Gandharvas, they were struck with wonder.
t.1.124.26: Suddenly the men there, by hundreds of thousands, their eyes wide open with wonder, cried out, "Well done! Well done!", O Bhārata.
t.1.124.27: Those mighty ones, having repeatedly practised the ways of the bow, of chariot-driving, of fighting on elephant-back and on horseback, and of wrestling,
t.1.124.28: Then, holding swords and shields, the strikers once more moved through the sword-hilt maneuvers as they had been taught, over every kind of ground.
t.1.124.29: There they beheld the agility, the skill, the grace, the steadiness, and the firmness of grip of them all in their handling of swords and shields.
t.1.124.30: Then Suyodhana and Vṛkodara, both ever thrilling with eagerness, descended into the arena, maces in hand, like two single-peaked mountains.
t.1.124.32: Those two mighty ones, bearing gleaming maces, moved in circles to the right and to the left, like two bulls in rut.
t.1.124.31: The two mighty-armed ones, their girdles tightly bound and firmly set upon their manly valor, were trumpeting like two rutting elephants fighting over a she-elephant.
t.1.124.33: Vidura and the mother of the Pāṇḍavas, the fire-stick from which they were kindled, reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī everything the princes had done.
